channel.title: GoodsInfinite Pet — Care Journal
channel.description: Vet-informed dog & cat care guides and answers.

item.title: Dog Scooting & Anal Glands: What's Normal, When to Help
item.description: Dog scooting on the floor often points to full anal glands. Learn why glands fill, how they're expressed, and the signs that mean a vet visit, not a guess at home.

item.title: Dog Conjunctivitis: Pink Eye, Discharge & When to Worry
item.description: Dog conjunctivitis (pink eye) causes red, weepy eyes and discharge. Learn the common causes, home-care limits, and when to see a vet fast to protect vision.

item.title: Puppy Teething: When Baby Teeth Fall Out & How to Help
item.description: Puppy teething starts around 3-4 months. Learn when baby teeth fall out, how to soothe sore gums safely, and the red flags that mean an early vet check.

item.title: Dog Cloudy Eye: Cataracts vs. Aging and When to Worry
item.description: A cloudy dog eye can be normal aging (nuclear sclerosis) or a cataract that needs care. Learn the difference and the red flags that mean an urgent vet visit.

item.title: How to Trim Cat Nails at Home: A Calm, Step-by-Step Method
item.description: Trimming your cat's nails at home prevents snags and saves furniture. A vet-informed, low-stress step-by-step — plus when a scratch or bleed means a vet visit.

item.title: Puppy Biting and Nipping: Stop It Before It Sticks
item.description: Puppy biting and nipping is normal teething, not aggression. Learn why it happens and 5 vet-informed ways to redirect it — plus when mouthing means a vet visit.

item.title: Dog Ear Infection: 6 Signs and When to See a Vet
item.description: Ear infections are a top reason dogs visit the vet. Spot the 6 early signs — head shaking, odor, redness — and know which symptoms mean you should see a vet fast.

item.title: How Often Should You Bathe Your Dog? A Coat-Type Guide
item.description: Bathing too often strips protective oils; too rarely lets odor and skin issues build. Find the right bath frequency for your dog's coat type, plus safe drying tips.

item.title: How to Clean Dog Tear Stains: A Safe Daily Routine
item.description: Light-coated dogs often get reddish-brown tear stains. A gentle daily cleanse keeps the under-eye zone dry and healthy — and flags when staining is a real vet problem.

item.title: Dog Dental Disease: 6 Warning Signs You Can Spot at Home
item.description: Most dogs show dental disease by age three. Spot 6 early signs at home - bad breath, red gums, trouble eating - and when bleeding gums mean a vet visit.

item.title: Dog Separation Anxiety: Signs, Causes & First Steps
item.description: Is your dog destructive or panicked when you leave? Learn the signs of separation anxiety, why it happens, and force-free first steps that calm a distressed dog.

item.title: Hot Spots on Dogs: Fast Relief and When to See a Vet
item.description: Hot spots are painful, fast-spreading skin sores. Learn what causes them, safe first-aid at home, and the red flags that mean your dog needs a vet now.

item.title: Dog Red Eye: 7 Causes and When It's a Real Emergency
item.description: A red eye in dogs can be harmless or an emergency. Learn the 7 common causes, how to tell them apart at home, and the signs that mean rush to the vet.

item.title: Cracked, Dry Dog Paws? How to Protect Pads Year-Round
item.description: Dry, cracked paw pads are painful and easy to miss. Learn what causes them, how to protect your dog's paws year-round, and the signs that mean it's time for the vet.

item.title: How to Brush Your Cat's Teeth: A No-Stress Weekly Plan
item.description: Most cats never get their teeth brushed, yet daily care prevents painful dental disease. Here's a calm, step-by-step plan that actually works on real cats.

item.title: Dog Not Drinking Water? Causes & When to Call a Vet
item.description: Refusing water can be normal for a day or a red flag. Here are the common reasons dogs skip the bowl, how much they need daily, and the warning signs to watch.

item.title: How to Deshed Your Dog and Cut Loose Fur at Home
item.description: Shedding is normal, but loose fur everywhere is not inevitable. A vet-informed deshedding routine — tools, bath timing and diet — that actually reduces the fur on your floor.

item.title: How to Socialize a Puppy: A Safe Week-by-Week Plan
item.description: A calm, confident adult dog starts with early socialization. A vet-informed week-by-week plan for safe exposure, what to avoid, and the signs your puppy is overwhelmed.

item.title: Do Dental Chews Actually Clean Dogs' Teeth? (The Truth)
item.description: Dental chews help but don't replace brushing. Learn what the research shows, how to pick a VOHC-accepted chew, and the red flags that mean a vet visit.

item.title: How to Trim Your Dog's Nails at Home (No Panic)
item.description: A calm, step-by-step guide to trimming dog nails at home — what tools to use, how to avoid the quick, and the signs you've gone too far.

item.title: Why Does My Cat Have Eye Discharge? Causes & Care
item.description: Cat eye discharge ranges from harmless sleep crust to infection. Learn the common causes, safe at-home cleaning, and the warning signs that mean a vet visit.

item.title: How to Clean Your Dog's Ears at Home (Safely, Step by Step)
item.description: A vet-informed, step-by-step guide to cleaning your dog's ears at home — what to use, what to avoid, how often, and the warning signs that mean an ear is infected.

item.title: Why Does My Dog Bark at Everything? Calming Reactive Barking
item.description: Reactive barking isn't defiance — it's an overwhelmed dog. Practical, force-free steps to lower the volume, reduce the stress, and reclaim a calmer home.

item.title: Why Is My Dog So Itchy? 6 Common Causes of Scratching
item.description: Dog scratching constantly? We break down 6 common causes of itchy skin — from dry air to parasites — plus the red flags that mean it's time for the vet.

item.title: How Often Should You Brush Your Dog's Teeth?
item.description: Vet-informed guidance on brushing frequency, what to do if your dog fights the brush, and how water additives and sprays fill the gap — without a wrestling match.

item.title: Moving With a Cat: A Vet-Informed Stress-Reduction Plan
item.description: Cats read the world through scent and territory. A practical, evidence-minded plan to cut moving-day anxiety — before, during and after the move.

item.title: Why Do Dogs Get Tear Stains — and What Actually Helps?
item.description: The science behind reddish under-eye stains in dogs, which breeds are prone, a safe daily routine, and the red flags that mean it's time for the vet.
